questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was able to take courses that were not offered at my home institute, thereby helping me to broaden my academic horizon. I was able to take the courses in English, thus being on an equal footing with my fellow students. I was able to live in a city and a country I have never visited before, and by knowing the language beforehand, I was able to fully partake in the culture and quickly make new friendships.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I was very poorly informed before going on my exchange. It also seemed to me as if there was no communication between my host and my home university leaving me in a very awkward middle position. It also seemed as if the procedure of my host institute and the procedure of the Erasmus program was not a line. When I arrived I was not assigned a single course and it took a long and tough battle with the visiting student office for me to get the courses I applied for, and I still only got 2 out of 3.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was assigned a personal tutor, but she was very limited in how much she could help me since all things related to my exchange had to go through the visiting student office.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments

questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through flatshare half an hour away from campus. It was fine, nothing to complain about.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: To lookout for possible housing in good time before going on exchange.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The process was very confusing with one having to apply for several times, I only got mine after a long correspondence with the visiting student office.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end, I got 2 out of 3 courses. But first, after the semester had been going on for 2 weeks.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be very aware of possible complications, and that you have to apply several times, also during the summer holiday.

Additional comments:

questions.answer: Each course was equivalent to 10 ECTS.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The quality of the lectures was approximately the same level, the professor though were only acquainted with the Anglo-Saxon philosophical tradition, and did not know much about continental philosophy.

questions.answer: Many, both sport, cultural, academic, and religious activities and societies were available for students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you're Catholic I can heavily recommend the Catholic Student Union (CSU) at the Dominican Chaplaincy at George Square. It's a very open and friendly environment open for members at all times, and it has a lot of activities during the week. People are very friendly and outgoing.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the Highland. If possible climb a Monroe or walk one of the great hiking routes in the Highland.

questions.answer: Become part of a society and engage with the locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *

questions.answer: The friendliness and openness, especially when going to the pub.

questions.answer:
Be aware of possible administrative mess. 
Enjoy going to the pub.
Become member of a society and engage with the locals.
